description: A service or admin panel is reachable using vendor-shipped default credentials (e.g. admin/admin, admin/password, root/root) that were never changed after installation.
impact: Direct, effortless authenticated access to the affected system — often full administrative control — with no exploitation required beyond trying well-known, publicly documented credential pairs.
remediation: Change every default credential immediately upon installation, before the system is ever network-reachable.
Where possible, force a credential change on first login rather than relying on documentation alone.
Enforce a minimum password policy that default credentials like 'admin'/'password' cannot satisfy.
Monitor authentication logs for successful logins using known default usernames.

audience_guidance.student: Many devices and applications ship with a preset username and password so you can log in the first time — the problem is when that default is never changed, and it's publicly documented, so anyone can look it up and log in too.
audience_guidance.developer: Force a credential change on first login in anything you build that ships with a default account, rather than trusting users to read the documentation and change it themselves.
audience_guidance.bug_bounty_hunter: Default credentials are one of the highest-value, lowest-effort checks in recon — always try the vendor's documented defaults for any identified product before moving on.
audience_guidance.pentester: Attempt documented default credentials for every identified product/service as a standard early step, and document exactly which pair worked as concrete, reproducible impact.
audience_guidance.security_team: Include a default-credential check in every new-system provisioning checklist, and periodically re-scan the environment for accounts still using vendor defaults.
